title: AI agent teams waste massive tokens for barely measurable quality gains, research finds
source_used: The Decoder (fulltext fetched by main session)
key_facts: The evaluation company Vals AI tested GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 on its Vibe Code Bench, each alone and as a team, at medium and maximum reasoning effort.
The teams cost between 1.8x and 5.1x more than single agents.
Of four team-versus-solo comparisons, only one was statistically significant: GPT-6 Sol at medium reasoning, where the team scored 7.3 points higher.
At maximum reasoning the team setup gave neither Sol nor Opus 5.5 any real advantage; the results suggest the extra cost is not worth it in most cases.
Anthropic saw quality gains shrink as it added more agents in two of its own tests with Opus 5.5; going from ten to 100 agents only nudged scores up slightly after 24 hours.
OpenAI researcher Noam Brown said on the Dwarkesh Podcast that multi-agent systems mainly buy speed, not better quality: four agents solved tasks twice as fast at twice the cost.
Brown said the effect depends on the task: web research and math parallelize well, writing a novel does not.
OpenAI developer Eric Provencher warned that agent swarms are most likely wasted money because coordination between agents breaks down.
